questions.q: Why does check_endpoint() pass a `timeout` to requests.get() instead of calling it without one?
options: Timeouts make the HTTP response arrive faster
Without a timeout, requests.get() can hang indefinitely on an unresponsive server, turning the health check itself into a hang
timeout is required syntax and has no functional effect
It converts the response into JSON automatically
questions.explain: A server that has stopped responding, rather than returning an error, can leave requests.get() waiting forever with no timeout set. The timeout guarantees the check itself fails fast instead of hanging.

questions.q: What does shutil.disk_usage() check, and why doesn't it need a network request?
options: It checks a remote server's disk space over SSH
It reads total, used, and free bytes for a local path directly from the filesystem, since disk space is a local resource, not a network-dependent one
It checks disk space only inside Docker containers
It requires a Slack webhook to function
questions.explain: Disk space is a property of the local filesystem, so shutil.disk_usage() reads it directly without any HTTP call -- unlike the endpoint check, which has to go over the network.

questions.q: Why does the Slack alert function read SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL from an environment variable instead of hardcoding it in the script?
options: Environment variables make the script run faster
A Slack webhook URL is a credential -- anyone who has it can post as Northbridge's monitoring, so it follows the same secrets-handling rule as other credentials in this course
Slack webhooks only work when read from an environment variable
Hardcoding strings is a Python syntax error
questions.explain: Anyone who obtains the webhook URL can post messages through it, which makes it a credential like any API key or token -- so it belongs in an environment variable, not hardcoded in source code.

questions.q: What problem does "alert on change, not on every check" solve?
options: It makes the health check run faster
Alert fatigue -- without it, a 15-minute check on an ongoing outage would send the same alert dozens of times a day until people stop reading them
It reduces the accuracy of the health check
It removes the need for a timeout on requests.get()
questions.explain: A check that alerts every time it runs, rather than only when the state flips, will repeat the same message every 15 minutes during a prolonged outage -- and people tune out alerts that repeat that often.

questions.q: In check_and_alert(), what triggers sending a message -- is_healthy being False, or something else?
options: is_healthy being False on its own, every time the check runs
is_healthy differing from the previously stored state (was_healthy), whether that's a failure or a recovery
The function sends an alert on every single call regardless of status
Only the disk-space check can ever trigger an alert
questions.explain: The function compares the current is_healthy to the previously stored was_healthy and only alerts when they differ -- covering both the DOWN transition and the RECOVERED transition, not a failing status by itself.
